title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 99 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 522–524 (Night 99, continuing directly from nights-98), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 99 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharrukān, down to twenty-five men, holds the cave until the infidels pile wood at its mouth and set it alight; the Muslims surrender, and the patrician keeps them alive to be killed before King Afrīdūn in Constantinople. That night the infidels drink themselves senseless. Sharrukān bursts his bonds, frees his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the vizier Dandān and the rest, and they slip away on the enemy's own horses; back with his men, Sharrukān has them all cry “God is greatest” from the mountain top. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِى أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَلَكُوا بَابَ الْمَغَارَةِ وَوَقَفُوا فِي طَرَفَيْهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna ʿaskara al-muslimīna malakū bāba al-maghārati wa-waqafū fī ṭarafayhi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the army of the Muslims held the door of the cave and stood at its two sides,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the Muslim army held the mouth of the cave, posted on either side of it,
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and ان together (السعيدان), as it often does; the spacing is kept. ṭarafayhi is the dual, “its two ends, its two sides”.

sentences.t: وَصَارُوا يَدْفَعُونَ الْكُفَّارَ عَنِ الْبَابِ وَكُلُّ مَنْ أَرَادَأَنْ يَهْجُمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَتَلُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārū yadfaʿūna al-kuffāra ʿani al-bābi wa-kullu man arāda an yahjuma ʿalayhim qatalūhu
sentences.l: and they began to push the infidels from the door, and every-one who wanted to rush upon them, they killed him.
sentences.i: and kept driving the infidels back from the entrance; whoever tried to rush them, they killed.
sentences.n: The print runs اراد and ان together (ارادان); the spacing is kept. kullu man … qatalūhu: the phrase is put first and picked up again by the -hu, “every one who …, they killed him”. hajama ʿalā, “rush upon, attack”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: وَصَبَرُوا عَلَى قِتَالِ الْكُفَّارِ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣabarū ʿalā qitāli al-kuffāri ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: And they endured in the fighting of the infidels until the day turned-away and the night came-on with the darkening.
sentences.i: They held out against the infidels until the day had turned away and the night came on in its darkness.
sentences.n: The same rhyming phrase closed the last night (with dhahaba, “went”, for wallā here): al-nahāru/al-iʿtikāri. aqbala bi-, “come on with”: bi- of what it brings.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَبْقَ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانَ إِلَّا خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ رَجُلًا لَاغَيْرُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yabqa ʿinda al-maliki sharrukāna illā khamsatun wa-ʿishrūna rajulan lā ghayru
sentences.l: And there remained not with King Sharrukān except five and twenty men, no other.
sentences.i: And King Sharrukān had no more than twenty-five men left, not one more.
sentences.n: The print sets لا غير as one word (لاغير); the spacing is kept. lā ghayru, “no other, only”, is a fixed tag after a number.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْكُفَّارُ لِبَعْضِهِمْ مَتَى تَنْقَضِي هَذِهِ الْأَيَّامُ فَإِنَّنَا قَدْ تَعِبْنَا مِنْ قِتَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-kuffāru li-baʿḍihim matā tanqaḍī hādhihi al-ayyāmu fa-innanā qad taʿibnā min qitāli al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And the infidels said to some-of-them: When will these days be-finished? For we have grown-tired of the fighting of the Muslims.
sentences.i: The infidels said to one another, “When will these days ever end? We are worn out with fighting the Muslims.”
sentences.n: li-baʿḍihim, “to one another”: li- marks whom they speak to.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ قُومُوا نَهْجُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ رَجُلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla baʿḍuhum qūmū nahjum ʿalayhim fa-innahu lam yabqa minhum illā khamsatun wa-ʿishrūna rajulan
sentences.l: And some-of-them said: Rise, let-us-rush upon them, for there remains not of them except five and twenty men.
sentences.i: Some of them said, “Up, let us fall on them; there are only twenty-five of them left.
sentences.n: nahjum is jussive, answering the command qūmū: “rise, (and) we shall attack”.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ لَمْ نَقْدِرْ عَلَيْهِمْ نُضْرِمْ عَلَيْهِمُ النَّارَ فَإِنِ انْقَادُوا وَسَلَّمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ إِلَيْنَا أَخَذْنَاهُمْ أَسَارَى وَإِنْ أَبَوْا تَرَكْنَاهُمْ حَطَبًا لِلنَّارِ حَتَّى يَصِيرُوا عِبْرَةً لِأُولِى الْأَبْصَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-in lam naqdir ʿalayhim nuḍrim ʿalayhimu al-nāra fa-ini inqādū wa-sallamū anfusahum ilaynā akhadhnāhum asārā wa-in abaw taraknāhum ḥaṭaban li-al-nāri ḥattā yaṣīrū ʿibratan li-ulī al-abṣāri
sentences.l: And if we are not able over them, we-kindle upon them the fire; and if they submit and hand themselves to us, we-take them captives, and if they refuse, we-leave them firewood for the fire, until they become a lesson for the possessors of the eyes.
sentences.i: If we cannot master them, we will set fire to them; if they give in and surrender themselves to us, we will take them prisoner, and if they refuse, we will leave them as kindling for the fire, until they are made a lesson for all who have eyes to see.
sentences.n: qadara ʿalā, “be able to deal with, overcome”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. li-ulī al-abṣāri, “for those possessed of sight”, is Qurʾānic: Q 3:13 and 24:44 have the very words la-ʿibratan li-ulī al-abṣāri, “a lesson for those possessed of sight”; li-, “for”. Sajʿ: al-nāri/al-abṣāri.

sentences.t: فَلَا رَحِمَ الْمَسِيحُ أَبَاهُمْ وَلَا جَعَلُ مُسْتَقَرَّ النَّصَارَى مَثْوَاهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lā raḥima al-masīḥu abāhum wa-lā jaʿalu mustaqarra al-naṣārā mathwāhum
sentences.l: So may the Messiah not have-mercy on their father, nor make the resting-place of the Christians their abode!
sentences.i: May the Messiah have no mercy on their father, and never make the Christians’ resting-place their abode!”
sentences.n: A curse in the infidels’ own mouths: lā with the past tense wishes, “may he not …”. They wish the Muslims shut out of the Christians’ heaven. The print sets a ḍamma on the last letter of جعل; the verb is jaʿala, but the printed mark is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ حَمَلُوا الْحَطَبَ إِلَى بَابِ الْمَغَارَةِ وَأَضْرَمُوا فِيهِ النَّارَ فَأَيْقَنَ شَرْكَانُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ بِالْبَوَارِ فَسَلَّمُوا نُفُوسَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum ḥamalū al-ḥaṭaba ilā bābi al-maghārati wa-aḍramū fīhi al-nāra fa-ayqana sharrukānu wa-man maʿahu bi-al-bawāri fa-sallamū nufūsahum
sentences.l: Then they carried the firewood to the door of the cave and kindled in it the fire; and Sharrukān and who was with him were certain of the perdition, and they surrendered themselves.
sentences.i: Then they carried the wood to the mouth of the cave and set it alight. Sharrukān and those with him were sure that they were lost, and gave themselves up.
sentences.n: ayqana bi-, “be certain of”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِالْبِطْرِيقِ الرَّئِيسِ عَلَيْهِمُ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى الْمُشِيرِ بِقَتْلِهِمْ فَقَالَ لَهُ لَا يَكُونُ قَتْلُهُمْ إِلَّا عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَ غَلِيلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-al-biṭrīqi al-raʾīsi ʿalayhimu iltafata ilā al-mushīri bi-qatlihim fa-qāla lahu lā yakūnu qatluhum illā ʿinda al-maliki afrīdūna li-ajli an yashfiya ghalīlahu
sentences.l: And while they were thus, and behold, the patrician, the chief over them, turned to the one advising their killing and said to him: Their killing shall not be except in-the-presence-of King Afrīdūn, for-the-sake that he may heal his burning-thirst.
sentences.i: While they were so, the patrician who commanded them turned to the man who was urging that they be killed, and said to him, “They are to be killed nowhere but before King Afrīdūn, so that he may slake his thirst for vengeance.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears. al-mushīr bi-qatlihim, “the one advising their killing”: ashāra bi-, “advise, counsel (a course)”, the verb chooses the bi-. shafā ghalīlahu, literally “heal his burning thirst”, is to have one’s revenge.

sentences.t: فَيَنْبَغِي أَنَّنَا نُبْقِيهِمْ عِنْدَنَا أَسَارَى وَفِي غَدٍ نُسَافِرُ بِهِمْ إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَنُسَلِّمُهُمْ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ فَيَفْعَلُ بِهِمْ مَا يُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-yanbaghī annanā nubqīhim ʿindanā asārā wa-fī ghadin nusāfiru bihim ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-nusallimuhum ilā al-maliki afrīdūna fa-yafʿalu bihim mā yurīdu
sentences.l: So it is fitting that we keep them with us captives, and on the morrow we travel with them to Constantinople and hand them to King Afrīdūn, and he does with them what he wants.
sentences.i: We ought to keep them here as prisoners, and tomorrow take them with us to Constantinople and hand them over to King Afrīdūn, to do with them as he pleases.”
sentences.n: yanbaghī annanā nubqīhim, “it is fitting that we keep them”: annanā with the indicative, where Classical would say an nubqiyahum. sāfara bi-, “travel with, take along”: bi- of company; faʿala bi-, “do to”.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا هَذَا هُوَ الرَّأْىُ الصَّوَابُ ثُمَّ أَمَرُوا بِتَكْتِيفِهِمْ وَجَعَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حُرَّاسًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālū hādhā huwa al-raʾyu al-ṣawābu thumma amarū bi-taktīfihim wa-jaʿalū ʿalayhim ḥurrāsan
sentences.l: And they said: This is the counsel, the right-one. Then they commanded the binding-of-their-arms, and set over them guards.
sentences.i: “That is the right course,” they said. Then they gave orders for their arms to be bound behind them, and set guards over them.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “command (something)”: the verb chooses the bi-. taktīf is tying the arms back at the shoulders (katif, “shoulder”).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ الظَّلَامُ اشْتَغَلَ الْكُفَّارُ بِاللَّهْوِ وَالطَّعَامِ وَدَعَوْا بِالشَّرَابِ فَشَرِبُوا حَتَّى انْقَلَبَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمْ عَلَى قَفَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā janna al-ẓalāmu ishtaghala al-kuffāru bi-al-lahwi wa-al-ṭaʿāmi wa-daʿaw bi-al-sharābi fa-sharibū ḥattā inqalaba kullun minhum ʿalā qafāhu
sentences.l: And when the darkness fell, the infidels busied-themselves with the amusement and the food, and called for the drink, and drank until each of them turned-over on the back-of-his-neck.
sentences.i: When darkness fell, the infidels gave themselves up to amusement and eating, and called for wine, and drank until every one of them had toppled over on his back.
sentences.n: The print has حنّ, a misprint for جنّ (“the darkness fell”), corrected here; the shadda is the print’s. ishtaghala bi-, “be busy with”; daʿā bi-, “call for (something)”: in both the verb chooses the bi-. Sajʿ: al-ẓalāmu/al-ṭaʿāmi.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ شَرْكَانُ وَأَخُوهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ مُقَيَّدَيْنِ وَكَذَلِكَ مَنْ مَعَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَبْطَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna sharrukānu wa-akhūhu ḍawʾu al-makāni muqayyadayni wa-ka-dhālika man maʿahum mina al-abṭāli
sentences.l: And Sharrukān and his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān were fettered-both, and likewise who was with them of the champions.
sentences.i: Sharrukān and his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān lay in fetters, and so did the warriors with them.
sentences.n: kāna is singular before a pair of subjects, as usual when the verb comes first; muqayyadayni, the dual, agrees with the two of them.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَظَرَ شَرْكَانُ إِلَى أَخِيهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي كَيْفَ الْخَلَاصُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika naẓara sharrukānu ilā akhīhi wa-qāla lahu yā akhī kayfa al-khalāṣu
sentences.l: And at that, Sharrukān looked at his brother and said to him: O my brother, how is the deliverance?
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān looked at his brother and said, “O my brother, how are we to get free?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَدْرِي وَقَدْ صِرْنَا كَالطَّيْرِ فِى الْأَقْفَاصِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-allāhi lā adrī wa-qad ṣirnā ka-al-ṭayri fī al-aqfāṣi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: By God, I do not know, and we have become like the birds in the cages.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “By God, I do not know; we have become like birds in cages.”
sentences.n: ka-, “like”. Sajʿ: al-khalāṣu/al-aqfāṣi, across the two speakers.

sentences.t: فَاغْتَاظَ شَرْكَانُ وَتَنَهَّدَ مِنْ شِدَّةِ غَيْظِهِ وَتَمَطَّى فَانْقَطَعَ الْكِتَافُ
sentences.tr: fa-ightāẓa sharrukānu wa-tanahhada min shiddati ghayẓihi wa-tamaṭṭā fa-inqaṭaʿa al-kitāfu
sentences.l: And Sharrukān grew-furious, and sighed from the vehemence of his fury, and stretched-himself, and the arm-bond snapped.
sentences.i: Sharrukān was seized with rage; he heaved a sigh from the force of his anger and strained his limbs, and the cord that bound his arms snapped.
sentences.n: kitāf is the rope that ties the arms back at the shoulders, from the same root as taktīf above.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَلَصَ مِنَ الْوَثَاقِ قَامَ إِلَى رَئِيسِ الْحُرَّاسِ وَأَخَذَ مَفَاتِيحَ الْقُيُودِ مِنْ جَيْبِهِ وَفَكَّ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَفَكَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ وَفَكَّ بَقِيَّةَ الْعَسْكَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā khalaṣa mina al-wathāqi qāma ilā raʾīsi al-ḥurrāsi wa-akhadha mafātīḥa al-quyūdi min jaybihi wa-fakka ḍawʾa al-makāni wa-fakka al-wazīra dandāna wa-fakka baqiyyata al-ʿaskari
sentences.l: And when he was free from the bond, he rose to the chief of the guards and took the keys of the fetters from his pocket, and loosed Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and loosed the vizier Dandān, and loosed the rest of the army.
sentences.i: Once free of his bonds, he went over to the captain of the guard, took the keys of the fetters from his pocket, and set loose Ḍawʾ al-Makān, then the vizier Dandān, then the rest of the soldiers.
sentences.n: jayb is the opening at the breast of a garment, where things were carried; “pocket” is near enough.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى أَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَقَالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ أَقْتُلَ مِنَ الْحُرَّاسِ ثَلٰثَةً وَنَأْخُذَ ثِيَابَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata ilā akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-al-wazīri dandāna wa-qāla innī urīdu an aqtula mina al-ḥurrāsi thalāthatan wa-naʾkhudha thiyābahum
sentences.l: Then he turned to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān and said: I want that I kill of the guards three, and we take their clothes,
sentences.i: Then he turned to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān and said, “I mean to kill three of the guards, and we will take their clothes
sentences.n: The print runs اريد and ان together (اريدان); the spacing is kept. ثلثة for thalātha is the edition’s regular spelling, without the long alif.

sentences.t: وَنَلْبَسَهَا نَحْنُ الثَّلٰثَةُ حَتَّى نَصِيرَ فِي زِيِّ الرُّومِ وَنَسِيرَ بَيْنَهُمْ حَتَّى لَا يَعْرِفُوا أَحَدًا مِنَّا ثُمَّ نَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى عَسْكَرِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-nalbasahā naḥnu al-thalāthatu ḥattā naṣīra fī ziyyi al-rūmi wa-nasīra baynahum ḥattā lā yaʿrifū aḥadan minnā thumma natawajjaha ilā ʿaskarinā
sentences.l: and we put them on, we the three, so that we become in the garb of the Rūm, and go among them so that they do not know any-one of us; then we head to our army.
sentences.i: and put them on, the three of us, so that we are dressed as Rūm; then we can walk among them without any of us being recognised, and make our way back to our army.”
sentences.n: Rūm, “Romans”, are the Byzantines.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّأْيَ غَيْرُ صَوَابٍ لِأَنَّنَا إِذَا قَتَلْنَاهُمْ نَخَافُ أَنْ يَسْمَعَ أَحَدٌ شَخِيرَهُمْ فَتَنْتَبِهَ إِلَيْنَا الْكُفَّارُ فَيَقْتُلُونَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni inna hādhā al-raʾya ghayru ṣawābin li-annanā idhā qatalnāhum nakhāfu an yasmaʿa aḥadun shakhīrahum fa-tantabiha ilaynā al-kuffāru fa-yaqtulūnanā
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: This counsel is not right, because if we kill them, we fear that someone hears their death-rattle, and the infidels become-alert to us, and they kill us.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “That plan is not sound. If we kill them, we must fear that someone will hear their death-rattle; then the infidels will be on to us and kill us.
sentences.n: shakhīr is a snorting or rattling in the throat; here the noise of men dying. fa-yaqtulūnanā keeps the indicative where the chain of subjunctives would lead one to expect fa-yaqtulūnā: the text’s own grammar. li-anna, “because”.

sentences.t: وَالرَّأْيُ السَّدِيدُأَنْ نَسِيرَ إِلَى خَارِجِ الشِّعْبِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-raʾyu al-sadīdu an nasīra ilā khāriji al-shiʿbi
sentences.l: And the counsel, the sound-one, is that we go to the outside of the ravine.
sentences.i: The sound course is to get clear of the ravine.”
sentences.n: The print runs السديد and ان together (السديدان); the spacing is kept. shiʿb is a mountain pass or ravine.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابُوهُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ فَلَمَّا صَارُوا بَعِيدًا عَنِ الشِّعْبِ بِقَلِيلٍ رَأَوْا خَيْلًا مَرْبُوطَةً وَأَصْحَابُهَا نَائِمُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābūhu ilā dhālika fa-lammā ṣārū baʿīdan ʿani al-shiʿbi bi-qalīlin raʾaw khaylan marbūṭatan wa-aṣḥābuhā nāʾimūna
sentences.l: And they answered him to that; and when they were far from the ravine by a little, they saw horses tethered and their owners sleeping.
sentences.i: They agreed to this. When they had gone a little way from the ravine, they saw horses tethered, and their riders asleep.
sentences.n: ajāba ilā, “consent to”: the verb chooses the ilā. bi-qalīlin, “by a little”: bi- of the measure.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِأَخِيهِ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَأْخُذَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا جَوَادًا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْخُيُولِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu li-akhīhi yanbaghī an yaʾkhudha kullu wāḥidin minnā jawādan min hādhihi al-khuyūli
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said to his brother: It is fitting that each one of us take a steed from these horses.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said to his brother, “Each of us should take one of these horses.”

sentences.t: وَكَانُوا خَمْسَةً وَعِشْرِينَ رَجُلًا فَأَخَذُوا خَمْسَةً وَعِشْرِينَ جَوَادًا وَقَدْ أَلْقَى اللَّهُ النَّوْمَ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ لِحِكْمَةٍ يَعْلَمُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kānū khamsatan wa-ʿishrīna rajulan fa-akhadhū khamsatan wa-ʿishrīna jawādan wa-qad alqā allāhu al-nawma ʿalā al-kuffāri li-ḥikmatin yaʿlamuhā
sentences.l: And they were five and twenty men, and they took five and twenty steeds; and God had cast the sleep upon the infidels for a wisdom He knows.
sentences.i: There were twenty-five of them, and they took twenty-five horses; for God had cast sleep upon the infidels, for a purpose known to Him.
sentences.n: li-ḥikmatin, “for a wise purpose”: li- of purpose.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ جَعَلَ يَخْتَلِسُ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ السِّلَاحَ مِنَ السُّيُوفِ وَالرِّمَاحِ حَتَّى اكْتَفَى ثُمَّ رَكِبُوا الْخَيْلَ الَّتِي أَخَذُوهَا وَسَارُوا
sentences.tr: thumma inna sharrukāna jaʿala yakhtalisu mina al-kuffāri al-silāḥa mina al-suyūfi wa-al-rimāḥi ḥattā iktafā thumma rakibū al-khayla allatī akhadhūhā wa-sārū
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān set-about stealing from the infidels the weapons, of the swords and the lances, until he had enough; then they mounted the horses that they had taken, and went.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān set about filching weapons from the infidels, swords and lances, until he had enough; then they mounted the horses they had taken and rode off.
sentences.n: jaʿala with an imperfect, “set about doing”. min in min al-suyūfi says what the weapons were.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ فِي ظَنِّ الْكُفَّارِ أَنَّهُ لَا يَقْدِرُ أَحَدٌ عَلَى فِكَاكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخِيهِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُمَا مِنَ الْعَسَاكِرِ وَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى الْحُرُوبِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna fī ẓanni al-kuffāri annahu lā yaqdiru aḥadun ʿalā fikāki ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-akhīhi wa-man maʿahumā mina al-ʿasākiri wa-annahum lā yaqdirūna ʿalā al-ḥurūbi
sentences.l: And it was in the thought of the infidels that no one is able for the release of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother and who was with the two of them of the troops, and that they are not able for the wars.
sentences.i: The infidels had supposed that no one could free Ḍawʾ al-Makān, his brother and the soldiers with them, and that they were in no state to fight.
sentences.n: The print has معها, “with her”, a misprint for معهما, “with the two of them”, corrected here. qadara ʿalā, “be able to (do)”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَلَصُوا جَمِيعًا مِنَ الْأَسْرِ وَصَارُوا فِي أَمْنٍ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ وَصَلَ شَرْكَانُ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فَوَجَدَهُمْ فِي انْتِظَارِهِ وَاقِفِينَ عَلَى نَارٍوَهُمْ مِنْ أَجْلِهِ فِي غَايَةِ الِافْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā khalaṣū jamīʿan mina al-asri wa-ṣārū fī amnin mina al-kuffāri waṣala sharrukānu ilā aṣḥābihi fa-wajadahum fī intiẓārihi wāqifīna ʿalā nārin wa-hum min ajlihi fī ghāyati al-iftikāri
sentences.l: And when they were free all from the captivity and were in safety from the infidels, Sharrukān arrived at his companions, and found them in waiting-for-him, standing on a fire, and they on his account in the utmost of the worrying.
sentences.i: When they were all out of captivity and safe from the infidels, Sharrukān reached his own men and found them waiting for him as if on hot coals, in the utmost anxiety on his account.
sentences.n: The print runs نار and وهم together (ناروهم); the spacing is kept. wāqifīna ʿalā nārin, “standing on a fire”, is to be on tenterhooks. Sajʿ: intiẓārihi/al-iftikāri.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِمْ شَرْكَانُ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ لَا تَخَافُوا حَيْثُ سَتَرَنَا اللَّهُ وَلَكِنْ عِنْدِي رَأْىٌ وَلَعَلَّهُ صَوَابٌ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata ilayhim sharrukānu wa-qāla lahum lā takhāfū ḥaythu sataranā allāhu wa-lākin ʿindī raʾyun wa-laʿallahu ṣawābun
sentences.l: And Sharrukān turned to them and said to them: Do not fear, since God has covered us; but with me is a counsel, and perhaps it is right.
sentences.i: Sharrukān turned to them and said, “Have no fear, since God has kept us safe. But I have a plan, and it may be a good one.”
sentences.n: ḥaythu, “where”, here means “since, seeing that”, a common use in this text. satara, “cover, shield”: God has hidden them from harm.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا وَمَا هُوَ قَالَ أُرِيدُأَنْ تَطْلُعُوا فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ وَتُكَبِّرُوا كُلُّكُمْ تَكْبِيرَةً وَاحِدَةً وَتَقُولُوا لَقَدْ جَاءَتْكُمُ الْعَسَاكِرُ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةُ وَنَصِيحَ كُلُّنَا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً بِقَوْلِ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū wa-mā huwa qāla urīdu an taṭlaʿū fawqa al-jabali wa-tukabbirū kullukum takbīratan wāḥidatan wa-taqūlū laqad jāʾatkumu al-ʿasākiru al-islāmiyyatu wa-naṣīḥa kullunā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan bi-qawli allāhu akbaru
sentences.l: And they said: And what is it? He said: I want that you climb above the mountain and cry “God is greatest”, all of you, one crying, and say: The Islamic armies have come to you! — and we shout, all of us, one shout, with the saying “God is greatest”.
sentences.i: “What is it?” they asked. He said, “I want you to climb up the mountain and all of you raise the cry of Allāhu akbar together, and call out, ‘The armies of Islam are upon you!’ — all of us shouting with one voice, ‘God is greatest!’
sentences.n: The print runs اريد and ان together (اريدان); the spacing is kept. kabbara, “say Allāhu akbar”, and takbīra, one such cry, are from the same root as akbar. bi-qawli, “with the saying of”: bi- of the words they shout.

sentences.t: فَيَفْتَرِقُ الْجَمْعُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ لَهُمْ فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ حِيلَةً فَإِنَّهُمْ سُكَارَى
sentences.tr: fa-yaftariqu al-jamʿu min dhālika wa-lā yajidūna lahum fī hādhā al-waqti ḥīlatan fa-innahum sukārā
sentences.l: And the gathering will be-scattered from that, and they will not find for themselves at this time a stratagem, for they are drunk;
sentences.i: At that the whole host will break apart, and they will find no way out at such a time, for they are drunk.
sentences.n: lahum, “for themselves”: li- of the people a thing would serve; they will find no way out for their own sakes.

sentences.t: وَيَظُنُّونَ أَنَّ عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَحَاطُوا بِهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ وَاخْتَلَطُوا بِهِمْ فَيَقَعُونَ ضَرْبًا بِالسُّيُوفِ فِي بَعْضِهِمْ مِنْ دَهْشَةِ السُّكْرِ وَالنَّوْمِ فَنُقَطِّعُهُمْ بِسُيُوفِهِمْ وَيَدُورُ السَّيْفُ فِيهِمْ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-yaẓunnūna anna ʿaskara al-muslimīna aḥāṭū bihim min kulli jānibin wa-ikhtalaṭū bihim fa-yaqaʿūna ḍarban bi-al-suyūfi fī baʿḍihim min dahshati al-sukri wa-al-nawmi fa-nuqaṭṭiʿuhum bi-suyūfihim wa-yadūru al-sayfu fīhim ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: and they will think that the army of the Muslims has surrounded them from every side and mingled with them, and they will fall striking with the swords on one-another from the bewilderment of the drunkenness and the sleep; and we cut them to pieces with their swords, and the sword goes round among them until the morning.
sentences.i: They will think the Muslim army has surrounded them on every side and got in among them, and in the daze of drink and sleep they will fall to hacking at one another with their swords. We shall cut them down with their own swords, and the sword will go round among them until morning.”
sentences.n: aḥāṭa bi-, “surround”; ikhtalaṭa bi-, “mingle with”: in both the verb chooses the bi-. bi-al-suyūfi, “with the swords”: bi- of the instrument. ʿaskar, “army”, takes a plural verb (aḥāṭū), by sense.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّأْىَ غَيْرُ صَوَابٍ وَالصَّوَابُ أَنَّنَا نَسِيرُ إِلَى عَسْكَرِنَا وَلَا نَنْطِقُ بِكَلِمَةٍ لِأَنَّنَا إِنْ كَبَّرْنَا تَنَبَّهُوا لَنَا وَلَحِقُونَا فَلَمْ يَسْلَمْ مِنَّا أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni inna hādhā al-raʾya ghayru ṣawābin wa-al-ṣawābu annanā nasīru ilā ʿaskarinā wa-lā nanṭiqu bi-kalimatin li-annanā in kabbarnā tanabbahū lanā wa-laḥiqūnā fa-lam yaslam minnā aḥadun
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: This counsel is not right; and the right is that we go to our army and do not utter a word, because if we cry “God is greatest”, they will become-aware of us and overtake us, and not one of us will be safe.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “That plan is not sound. The right thing is to make for our own army without a word; for if we raise the cry, they will be alerted to us and catch us up, and not one of us will come through.”
sentences.n: naṭaqa bi-, “utter”: the verb chooses the bi-. tanabbaha li-, “become aware of”: li- of what they notice.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ وَاللَّهِ لَوِا نْتَبَهُوا لَنَا مَا عَلَيْنَا بَأْسٌ وَأَشْتَهِي أَنْ تُوَافِقُونِي عَلَى هَذَا الرَّأْىِ وَهُوَ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّاخَيْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu wa-allāhi law intabahū lanā mā ʿalaynā baʾsun wa-ashtahī an tuwāfiqūnī ʿalā hādhā al-raʾyi wa-huwa lā yakūnu illā khayran
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: By God, if they became-alert to us, there is no harm upon us; and I desire that you agree-with-me on this counsel, and it will not be except good.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said, “By God, even if they are alerted to us, we shall come to no harm. I would like you to go along with me in this plan; nothing but good will come of it.”
sentences.n: The print sets the space one letter late, لوا نتبهوا, for لو انتبهوا; the words are read as law intabahū and the printed spacing is kept. It also runs الا and خيرا together (الاخيرا). tuwāfiqūnī is the subjunctive after an (no -na), with -nī, “me”; wāfaqa ʿalā, “agree with (someone) on”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابُوهُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ وَطَلَعُوا فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ وَصَاحُوا بِالتَّكْبِيرِ فَكَبَّرَتْ مَعَهُمُ الْجِبَالُ وَالْأَشْجَارُ وَالْأَحْجَارُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābūhu ilā dhālika wa-ṭalaʿū fawqa al-jabali wa-ṣāḥū bi-al-takbīri fa-kabbarat maʿahumu al-jibālu wa-al-ashjāru wa-al-aḥjāru min khashyati allāhi
sentences.l: And they answered him to that, and climbed above the mountain and shouted with the takbīr; and with them the mountains and the trees and the stones cried “God is greatest”, from fear of God.
sentences.i: They agreed, climbed the mountain and shouted the takbīr, and the mountains, the trees and the stones cried “God is greatest” with them, in awe of God.
sentences.n: ṣāḥa bi-, “shout (a cry)”: bi- of the words shouted. The stones that fall down “from fear of God” are Qurʾānic (Q 2:74).

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ الْكُفَّارُ ذَلِكَ التَّكْبِيرَ فَصَاحَ الْكُفَّارُ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa al-kuffāru dhālika al-takbīra fa-ṣāḥa al-kuffāru
sentences.l: And the infidels heard that takbīr, and the infidels shouted —
sentences.i: The infidels heard that cry, and they shouted out —
sentences.n: The night breaks off mid-scene; the next night picks up the infidels’ cry.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
